# Ilium Plugin Developer Manual

> Developer manual for Ilium plugins: WebAssembly components (wasm32-wasip2) written in Rust or TypeScript that add tree decorations, commands, settings, panels, pane kinds, widgets and ambient scenes to the Ilium terminal multiplexer. The contract is the WIT package plus the manifest.

Every page below is also served as plain Markdown at the same address with `.md` instead of the trailing slash. `llms-full.txt` holds the whole manual in one file. Ready-made agent instruction files for plugin projects are under `agent-kit/`.

## Start here

- [Plugin manual](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/landing.md): A plugin adds features to Ilium. It can decorate tree rows with badges, add commands and keybindings, add settings pages, open panels and dialogs, provide a pane kind, add toolbar buttons to agent panes, raise...
- [Your first plugin in five minutes](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/getting-started-first-plugin.md): This page takes you from an empty folder to a badge on an agent row. You create a server-side plugin from the template, change one line of Rust, and run the plugin in dev mode. The page shows the tree before and...
- [What a plugin is](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/getting-started-overview.md): Ilium splits its work into two parts. The kernel is the part that must not break. It owns the project tree, the pane processes, the terminal emulator, input routing and the saved state. A plugin adds behaviour on top...
- [Set up a toolchain](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/getting-started-toolchain.md): This page explains what you install to build a plugin in Rust or TypeScript, and what each ilium plugin command does with your source. A plugin is built as a WebAssembly component that targets WASI Preview 2. You...

## Core plugins

- [Core plugins](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugins.md): A core plugin is the plugin form of a feature Ilium has today. Ilium ships and maintains all 30 of them, and each one has an id of the form ilium.core.<name>. Where a feature is native to the kernel, such as starting...
- [Tree](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-tree.md): The Tree plugin (ilium.core.tree, side both) owns the project tree as the user sees it: groups, folders and top-level destinations, moving, renaming and closing entries, the tree order, bookmarks, locks and the...
- [Layout](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-layout.md): The Layout plugin (ilium.core.layout, side both) owns split views and the arrangement of panes on screen: splitting four ways, mixed splits of terminal, editor and board panes, focus and navigation, and resizing with...
- [Terminal](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-terminal.md): The Terminal plugin (ilium.core.terminal, side both) owns terminal panes as plugins see them: pane processes and their signals, screen reads, scrollback history, typed and pasted input, clickable links, pane titles...
- [Smart Copy](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-smart-copy.md): The Smart Copy plugin (ilium.core.smart-copy, side both) owns selection and copying in terminal panes: mouse selection of regions, the terminal right-click menu, Smart Copy light (paths, commands and hashes...
- [Editor](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-editor.md): The Editor plugin (ilium.core.editor, side client) owns editor panes: buffers, syntax highlighting through a token provider, line numbers and the minimap, Markdown source and rendered views, the file explorer and...
- [Kanban](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-kanban.md): The Kanban plugin has the id ilium.core.kanban and runs on the client side. It owns the board pane: a basic pane that draws cards in To do, Doing and Done columns. A board can be backed by a Markdown file. The plugin...
- [Agent detection](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-agent-detect.md): The Agent detection plugin has the id ilium.core.agent-detect and runs on both sides. The server side owns agent identity and activity: it identifies agent CLIs from the process tree, classifies what each agent is...
- [Agent toolbar](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-agent-toolbar.md): The Agent toolbar plugin has the id ilium.core.agent-toolbar and runs on both sides. It owns the per-agent chrome in the pane frame and the tree: the last-prompt banner, the toolbar and its actions, the model and...
- [Fleet](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-fleet.md): The Fleet plugin has the id ilium.core.fleet and runs on both sides. It owns work with many agents at once: messaging one agent or all of them, Ask for update, ilium panes, ilium broadcast, ilium new-pane and the...
- [Cost](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-cost.md): The Cost plugin has the id ilium.core.cost and runs on both sides. It owns spend and usage: session statistics and the stats dot, spend and quota indicators, sorting the tree by cost, the price table, reset forecasts...
- [Titles and organisation](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-titles.md): Titles and organisation is the plugin form of Ilium's AI naming and tree tidying. It turns each prompt you send to an agent into a short pane title, picks an icon for the row, names new sessions, and can reorganise...
- [Inference providers](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-inference.md): Inference providers is the plugin form of Ilium's AI provider layer. It answers every model request that another plugin makes with the inference import, lists the available models, streams replies, and offers a Test...
- [Notifications](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-notifications.md): Notifications is the plugin form of Ilium's alerts. It plays sounds for events, shows desktop notices, draws in-app toasts, merges bursts of redundant task alerts, and marks tree nodes that need you for the Attention...
- [Voice](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-voice.md): Voice is the plugin form of Ilium's voice control. Hold F8 or press the voice button, speak, and Ilium either runs one of its own commands or types a prompt into an agent, asking for confirmation when the action is...
- [Scheduler](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-scheduler.md): Scheduler is the plugin form of Ilium's delayed and queued input. It sends text to a pane after a countdown, even after a restart. It holds a prompt queue that delivers one prompt each time an agent finishes a turn....
- [Text triggers](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-text-triggers.md): Text triggers are regular-expression rules that watch terminal output and send text to the pane that printed it. A typical rule answers a confirmation prompt such as Continue? (y/n) with y. The plugin id is...
- [Progress](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-progress.md): Progress monitors let a long task show how far it is. An agent or a script registers a probe command with ilium progress set, the server runs the probe on an interval, and the tree and status bar show the result....
- [Chatroom](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-chatroom.md): The Chatroom is a shared message board for the agents of one project and for the user. Its messages live in a plain CHATROOM.md file at the project root, so every agent can read and append to it. The plugin id is...
- [Worktrees](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-worktrees.md): A worktree agent works in its own Git worktree, a second checkout of the repository on its own branch, so several agents can change the same project without stepping on each other. The plugin id is...
- [Sessions](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-sessions.md): A session is one project's tree of groups and panes together with the processes that run in it. Sessions outlive the terminal window: the user can detach and reattach, and after a restart the tree comes back from a...
- [Compaction](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-compaction.md): The Compaction plugin (id ilium.core.compaction, sides: server and client) is the plugin form of Ilium's context compaction. When an agent's context fills up, the plugin builds a summary of the transcript in a...
- [Settings](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-settings.md): The Settings plugin (id ilium.core.settings, side: client) is the plugin form of the Settings screen. It owns the tab strip, the auto-save behaviour, the guided setup shown on first run, the User Interface tab...
- [Keys and help](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-keys-and-help.md): The Keys and help plugin (id ilium.core.keys-and-help, side: client) is the plugin form of Ilium's keyboard and help surfaces. It draws the key reference, shows the prefix and the active preset, offers a key-capture...
- [Workspace search](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-search.md): The Workspace search plugin (id ilium.core.search, sides: server and client) is the plugin form of Ilium's workspace search. One panel finds agents, terminals and files by name, by the text on their screens, and by...
- [Ambient look](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-ambient.md): The Ambient look plugin (id ilium.core.ambient, side: client) is the plugin form of the shared look of animated backgrounds. It owns the colour, palette, dithering and display controls that every scene gets, the...
- [Scenes](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-scenes.md): The Scenes plugin (id ilium.core.scenes, side: scene) is the plugin form of the animated scenes themselves. A scene is a renderer that draws frames into a surface. The host runs it in its own animation world, applies...
- [Recap](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-recap.md): A recap is a few factual sentences about what one pane is doing, written once in a short form (at most 40 words) and once in a long form (at most 250 words). ilium recap prints them for every selected agent and shell...
- [Session conversion](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-session-convert.md): Session conversion lets a conversation continue under the other agent. A Claude Code conversation becomes a Codex conversation, or a Codex conversation becomes a Claude Code one, without starting over. The plugin id...
- [Agent setup](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/core-plugin-agent-setup.md): Agents work better in Ilium when their instruction files describe what Ilium offers. Agent setup installs two blocks of instructions into the files an agent reads at start. The Chatroom block tells agents how to talk...

## Concepts

- [Architecture](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/architecture.md): Ilium keeps the code that runs per byte, per keystroke or per frame in the kernel. Everything else that a feature needs can be a plugin. Plugins run inside a plugin host, behind a fixed contract, ilium:plugin@0.1.0,...
- [Background jobs](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/background-jobs.md): An event handler has a deadline of 20 ms by default, so it cannot parse a large file or search a whole workspace. A background job moves that work out of the handler. The plugin starts a job with a kind and an input...
- [Capabilities and grants](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/capabilities.md): A plugin can use only the parts of the host that it asks for. It lists the capabilities it needs in its manifest, one list per side. The user grants them when a package is installed or first activated. For bundled...
- [Debugging](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/debugging.md): A plugin problem shows up in one of four places: the plugin log, a trap, a deadline breach or the disabled notice in the tree footer. This page explains the log import and its levels, how to read ilium plugin logs,...
- [Errors and limits](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/errors-and-limits.md): A host call can fail in two ways. It can return a typed error that the plugin handles, or it can trap, which ends the plugin instance at once. A returned error is an ordinary result: Result<T, PluginError> in Rust,...
- [Events and intents](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/events-and-intents.md): A plugin learns what happens through events and changes the world through intents. The kernel delivers events in batches of at most 256. The handler answers each batch with a list of submissions, each carrying one...
- [File access](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/file-access.md): A plugin reaches files only through named scopes. A scope is a directory the user has granted, such as the project folder, or a directory the plugin owns, such as its private data folder. The kernel resolves each...
- [Layout constraints](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/layout.md): A plugin never works out where a widget goes. It describes the sizes it wants with constraints, and the host runs the solver of ratatui 0.29. This page gives the constraint kinds, the flex, spacing and margin rules,...
- [Lifecycle](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/lifecycle.md): A plugin moves through install, activation, running, stopping and, when something goes wrong, failure, revocation or disable. The host decides when each stage happens. Your code receives two calls, activate and...
- [Packages and manifests](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/packages.md): A plugin ships as one .iliumpkg file. It is a ZIP archive with a fixed layout and a manifest.json at its root. The manifest names the plugin, lists its components, states the grants it needs and declares what it adds...
- [Pane primitives](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/primitives.md): A pane holds one piece of content: a shell, an agent session, a text buffer or a widget tree. A primitive is the host-provided kind of pane that a plugin builds on. Ilium has four primitives: terminal, agent, editor...
- [Requests and outcomes](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/requests-and-outcomes.md): Some host calls take longer than a handler can wait. A handler has a deadline of 20 ms by default, so an HTTP request, a whole-file read or a process run cannot finish inside one on-events call. For those calls the...
- [Retained mode](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/retained-mode.md): Plugins do not draw on every frame. A plugin describes the state it wants, such as a badge on a tree row, a virtual row in the tree or the enabled state of an agent toolbar button. The kernel stores that state, draws...
- [Services](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/services.md): A service is a named interface that one plugin provides and other plugins call. The caller sends a method name and a JSON payload. The provider answers with a JSON reply, at once or later. The plugins never link to...
- [Extending core plugins](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/extending-core-plugins.md): Many features of Ilium are core plugins: titles, cost, fleet, notifications, search and more. Core plugins lists them. This page answers one question: how does another plugin control, change or build on one of those...
- [Testing plugins](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/testing.md): This page is the how-to. The exact contract of the harness, with every method, error code and limit, is Test harness reference. If this page and the reference differ, the reference wins.
- [The UI model](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/ui-model.md): A plugin describes its interface as a flat list of widgets. The kernel lays the list out, draws it with the Ilium theme, keeps the state of each widget and reports what the user did. The plugin never draws, and it...
- [Versioning](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/versioning.md): The plugin contract has a version. The host and each plugin declare the version they use, and the host decides at install whether it can load a package. This page explains the version identity of a package, the...
- [Worlds and sides](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/worlds-and-sides.md): A plugin package holds up to three components, one for each side of Ilium: server, client and scene. The server component runs in one host for each session server. The client component runs in one host for each...
- [Extending Settings](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/settings-extension.md): A plugin can put its own settings into Ilium's Settings screen. It can do that in two ways:

## Host API

- [audio](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-audio.md): The audio import lists the sound devices, opens a capture stream from a microphone or from a loopback of the desktop output, and plays samples. Captured audio arrives as audio-frames events, one event for each 20 ms...
- [cli](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-cli.md): The cli import lets a server-side plugin add a subcommand to the ilium command line. The plugin declares the subcommand in its manifest. When the user runs ilium <name> [arguments], the kernel routes the call to the...
- [clipboard](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-clipboard.md): The clipboard import reads and writes plain text on the system clipboard. The clipboard belongs to the user's desktop session, so the client runs this import and a server-side plugin cannot call it. Writing is common...
- [clock and timers](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-clock-and-timers.md): The clock import gives wall-clock time and monotonic time. The timers import fires a timer-fired event after a delay, and again at a fixed interval when you ask for one. A plugin uses clock to read the time and to...
- [codec](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-codec.md): The codec import does the byte-level work that plugins need without shipping their own libraries. It inflates and deflates data, reads image sizes, decodes images to RGBA pixels, computes SHA-256 digests and...
- [commands](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-commands.md): A command is a named action that a plugin contributes, such as "New note" or "Save note". The user runs a command from the command palette, a keybinding, a toolbar button, a context menu, a tree row action, a status...
- [Events](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-events.md): Events are what the kernel tells a plugin. The kernel queues them for each plugin and hands them over in batches to the handler export. Each call to on-events returns the submissions the plugin wants the kernel to...
- [Plugin exports](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-exports.md): A plugin imports host functions and also exports functions that the host calls. Each export belongs to one side of the plugin: server, client or scene. The host calls an export only when the feature it serves is...
- [fs](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-fs.md): The fs interface reads and writes files, but only inside file scopes. A scope is a named root that the user has granted, such as the project, a path the user picked, or the plugin's own data folder. Each call names a...
- [help and plugins](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-help-and-plugins.md): The help and plugins imports cover two related jobs. The help import reads the Markdown help topics that installed plugins ship in their packages. The plugins import lists every installed plugin and turns plugins on...
- [http](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-http.md): The http import sends an HTTP request to a host that the plugin has been granted, and it hands the response back to the plugin. A network call is slow, so the raw function returns a request-id at once. The response...
- [http-api](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-http-api.md): The http-api import lets a server-side plugin answer requests on the Ilium loopback HTTP listener. The kernel owns the listener, the socket, the token check and the request parsing. The plugin declares each route in...
- [inference](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-inference.md): The inference import sends a chat completion to the language model provider that the user selected in Settings. The plugin never names a provider. It names the feature that asks, through purpose, and the AI admission...
- [intents](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-intents.md): An intent is a request that asks the kernel to change something: rename a node, close a pane, type into a terminal, show a notice. A plugin never changes the tree, a pane or a window itself. It returns submissions...
- [jobs](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-jobs.md): A job is work that runs in the background, away from the plugin's event handler. The plugin starts a job with a kind and an input of bytes. The host runs the plugin's job-runner export in a second instance of the...
- [keys](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-keys.md): The keys import lets a client plugin take a key chord for itself. A call that takes a chord is a grab. While a grab is active, the keys it names go to the plugin as key-pressed events and do not reach the pane...
- [location](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-location.md): The location import returns the observer position that the user sets in Settings > Location. A plugin asks for it with one synchronous call and gets back a latitude and longitude pair, or nothing when the user has...
- [log](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-log.md): The log import writes one line to the plugin log at a level you choose. Each plugin has its own log. The user reads it with ilium plugin logs <id>. The host writes its own records into the same log, such as refused...
- [media](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-media.md): The media import decodes a video file into frames. The host decodes the file natively, outside the plugin, and keeps a small buffer of decoded frames ahead of the plugin's requests. The plugin opens a file, asks for...
- [Messages and topics](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-messages-and-topics.md): Messages and topics let plugins talk without calling each other. A message goes to one receiver: the other side of the same plugin, or a named peer plugin. A topic is a named channel that a plugin publishes on. Every...
- [Notifications and sounds](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/api-notifications.md): A plugin tells the user about an event in two ways. The notify intent shows a desktop notice, and the play-sound intent plays one sound from the sound catalogue. Both are submitted from the handler export, as the...

- [Agent transcript and signals](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/primitives-agent-transcript.md): The base agent primitive tells a plugin which agent runs in a pane and what it is doing. - [Capability table](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/reference-capabilities.md): A capability is a permission that unlocks one group of host functions or events. Every import a plugin can call, and every event it can receive, belongs to exactly one capability. The plugin lists the capabilities it...
- [Error codes and limits](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/reference-errors-and-limits.md): A plugin calls host functions, and some of those calls fail. A failed call returns a plugin-error record to the caller, and the plugin keeps running. A contract violation is different: it traps the plugin instance,...
- [Event and intent tables](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/reference-events-and-intents.md): Plugins hear about the world through events, and they change it through intents. - [Manifest reference](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/reference-manifest.md): The manifest is the manifest.json file at the root of every .iliumpkg package. The host reads it before any code runs. It names the plugin and its publisher, lists one WebAssembly component per side, requests grants,...
- [Core extension points](http://127.0.0.1:4327/pages/reference-core-extension-points.md): Every core plugin owns extension points, publishes services and topics, and says whether another plugin may replace it.
